title: Prepare the existing laptop upgrade safely
outcome: A reviewable provider-neutral runbook for updating the old home installation to the current tested Voice Fleet revision without losing existing data or pretending live voice acceptance.
acceptance: Create docs/home-upgrade.md with an explicit inventory/preparation phase, clearly separating historical evidence from unexecuted host checks.

Use the exact existing project voice-fleet-home, source /home/waks/projects/voice, old snapshot dcc59c9, target upstream 23c633e16dc5c9a9ed27f643852a5b1977c3b793, and named volume voice-fleet-home_db_data. Require verification of those values before mutation.

Provide concrete Linux commands to create a restricted custom-format PostgreSQL backup, verify it by restoring into a separately named disposable database, and compare schema plus synthetic/aggregate counts without exposing personal data or credentials.

Stage the target in a separate release directory; preserve the existing .env and home override without printing their contents; document migration 0002 through 0007, existing user/agent preservation checks, loopback origin, readiness, and explicitly unconfigured worker behavior.

Explain rollback as paired old code/images plus verified pre-upgrade DB restore in maintenance, not merely reverting code after forward migrations. Never down --volumes, destroy the real volume, downgrade schema automatically, create real accounts, enable paid services or make live API/SIP calls.

State current blocker accurately: SSH user waks lacks docker group access and sudo -n true reports a password is required. The owner must run privileged steps interactively; do not change permissions or sudoers.

Include executable check commands from the repository and manual acceptance (admin login, draft/publish/activate, restart persistence). Do not claim the upgrade, backup, restore, migrations or owner acceptance happened.
